<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5dfde742e692be735493cea980b13b44bd1204c7` — the merge of head `a27c4db8d80dcffae5cc8422c8e3927a7285ab36` into base `e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5dfde742e692be735493cea980b13b44bd1204c7 && git checkout 5dfde742e692be735493cea980b13b44bd1204c7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e a27c4db8d80dcffae5cc8422c8e3927a7285ab36 && git checkout -B drift-repro e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e && git merge --no-ff a27c4db8d80dcffae5cc8422c8e3927a7285ab36

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat note: `Test Core (3/6)` red on `306de5fe`, held for the post-stage-1 merge round

Epic PM `session_01Rerax7QTjKMPCUZxQUtPFR` (`marchtian`), seat `epic:#15194`, 2026-10-11T01:45Z.

**The failing check.** Job 114341427182 (run 38095818706) fails, along with the `Test Core` roll-up. The failing test is `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.boot-parity.integration.test.ts`, case "a host config — instances in plugins beside its own metadata, the showcase's shape", assertion `:136`. The plan returned a pending `create_table` for `sys_activity`, plugin-audit's object, after a boot with `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1`.

**Why the seat does not read it as this PR's:**
- This diff touches no object registration, boot composition or migrate code. It adds the activation route, the security-domain arm, gate entries and tests.
- The dev ran it on `306de5fe` with os-verify-lock:
  - cli integration: 109 files, 995 passed;
  - the test file alone: 3 runs in a row, each 3/3 green.
- Stage 1's merge group `bfc15d27` (`main` `ed1de8c2` + stage 1, which is this PR's base) ran all six `Test Core` shards green.
- The test reached `main` with #22732 (`7c7e7505`).

**What happens next.** No fix exists to port. The seat's relay cannot re-run jobs. So the next CI run comes from the post-stage-1 merge round: once #22723 merges, this PR retargets to `main` and the dev merges `origin/main` under landing-operations §A. If `Test Core (3/6)` reds again on that head with the same `sys_activity` row, the seat treats it as real and has it root-caused. If the cause lies outside this diff, it is raised as a proposed patch, not added to this PR.

Stage 2c of #15204 (amendment 6101897723; seat answers 6103293232; pin rule 6103398921; stage 1 ACCEPT 6102862135 and Landed 6104351995). Read on GitHub only: the card body and all 56 comments, the PR body, its 17-file list, the net diff against `main` `bfc15d27` (+1,174 / −73), the dev's report 6102842837 and merge-round addendum 6104607329, the seat note 6104322014, and the check-runs on this head. `main` was read for the gate bodies, the activation store, the catalog reader, the ledger object, the resolver's ledger read, the REST `/security` rows and the two docs pages.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The route's accept set — right, and the action door's exactly.** `POST /api/v1/security/_activation/:type/:name` (also under `/environments/:environmentId` when scoping is on) admits a caller iff: not anonymous (the `/security` domain floor answers 401 before the arm); `executionContext.isSystem` or `systemPermissions` holds `manage_metadata` (`refuseUngrantedActivationAuthoring`, else 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`); and either no `tenancy` service, a posture that enforces no wall, or `posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` (`refuseUngrantedActivationWrite`; a wall with a non-operator is 403, a `tenancy` that throws is the 503 outage). Both are the unchanged functions on `main`, with two new `ActivationSubject`s. Pinned per type in `catalog-activation-door.test.ts` (single · no tenancy · no capability · anonymous · group/isolated for the tenant admin and the operator) and in the shared outage pin (4 cases).
2. **No widening of who may write a position or permission set (#22621 → A) — right.** The door writes no definition and no catalog row: `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.setActive` touches `sys_metadata_activation` alone (find by `(metadata_type, name)`, update by id or insert). Its accept set is the metadata door's catalog-write authority (a system write, or `manage_metadata`), narrowed under a wall; an organization administrator without `manage_metadata` is refused in every posture. `sys_metadata_activation` keeps `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']`, so the data API still cannot write it: the ledger's writers are the three activation doors and system writes.
3. **Which `(metadata_type, name)` may be switched — right.** `:type` is closed to `position` | `permission`, the two `LEDGER_CATALOG_TYPES` the resolver reads (`capability` is the door's own 400). The name must resolve through `securityCatalogReaderOf(ql)`, the reader stage 1 binds and `resolveUserAuthzGrants` reads: registry first (platform sets, package manifests, the six built-in positions), then the metadata service; a definition owned by a disabled package resolves to nothing. Unknown → 404, no reader or a reader that throws → 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, no ledger object → 501. The row carries the definition's `_packageId`. Door and resolver therefore share one name space, which is what makes the resolver-effect pins (unit and booted showcase) evidence.
4. **What is refused — right, with one escalation.** (a) Both authority gates run before shape, body and lookup, so a refused caller learns neither the contract nor whether the name exists (pinned). (b) The last-admin guard: stage 1's `refuseLedgerSwitchingAdminOff` on `main` refuses `active: false` for `(permission, admin_full_access)` on insert and on update (re-reading the row by id when type and name are absent); the door surfaces the hook's own 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` and writes nothing, pinned on the real boot. That hook alone guards lockout on this head; its ruled replacement is 2b's (③.6). (c) **Anchor names `everyone` and `guest` are not refused.** Both are registered `position` items (`builtin-positions.ts` registers the six built-ins through `registerItem('position', …)`), so they resolve, and any `manage_metadata` holder under `single` may write `(position, everyone, active: false)`; the resolver honours it (stage 1's pin `off('position', 'everyone')` → `permissions: []`, `everyone` absent). That is a one-write, deployment-wide removal of the authenticated baseline. It adds no privilege, it is reversible by the same caller (whose standing rides `admin_full_access`, which the hook protects), and no ruling I was given forbids it: ADR-0090 D5/D9 is about privilege bits on the anchors, #22621 → A about definition writes, and the regime's switch is documented as an installation-wide incident-response control. Escalated in ③.7, not a FAIL reason.
5. **The anchor-guard carrier of 6102862135 — this door is not such a path.** The carrier binds "any later stage that opens an environment write path for an anchor definition". This door writes one `sys_metadata_activation` row and no definition; `describeAnchorForbiddenBits(def, anchor)` judges the bits a definition carries, and an activation row changes none. The anchors' definitions stay sealed exactly as stage 1 measured (`refusePackagedBaseOverride`, `allowOrgOverride: false`, `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`). No definition-write gate is owed here, and none is built.
6. **The public surface, enumerated — right.** One new HTTP route, `server-only`, route-ledger row 85 (census regenerated; the authz matrix docblock and the blind-spot census moved 84 → 85 with their controls, `reachable` with `population`, `blindSpot` 0). `activation-gate.ts` gains `readActivationBody`, `POSITION_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT` and `PERMISSION_SET_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT`; `catalog-activation.ts` is new. `actions.ts` now reads its body through the shared reader: the three refusal strings and the `VALIDATION_FAILED` envelope are byte-identical to the inline copy they replace, so the action door's contract does not move. The `security.ts` arm sits after the anonymous floor and before the `security` service probe, so the door serves on a composition without that service while every other `/security` path keeps today's answer (pinned: `/suggested-bindings` still 503 "Security service not available"). The dispatcher mounts the route at the three action-door call sites; the literal `_activation` collides with no REST `/security` row (`explain`, `my-delegable-scope`, `suggested-bindings/…`, `permission-sets/:id/discard-overlay`; none takes a parameter in that segment), and the booted case that sends `capability/manage_metadata` and gets the door's own 400 proves the wire reaches it.
7. **The amendment's exclusions hold.** No transition piece: the door reads the catalog reader and writes the ledger, with no row fallback, no junction read and no write-through. No retired module is touched. Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`. The lane is `runtime/src/domains/` plus the mount, the ledger, two scripts, the dogfood tests and three docs/comment files; nothing in `plugin-security/src`, `plugin-auth/src` or `plugin-sharing/src`, so no overlap with 2a or 2b.
8. **The merge round is a merge round.** The 14 stage-2c files are byte-identical, hunk for hunk, to `306de5fe` (compared file by file). The net diff against `main` `bfc15d27` holds those 14 plus `authorization.mdx`, `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` and `row-active.ts`; no stage 1 file appears in it, and the one conflict (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`) resolved to `main`'s deletion, so it is absent. The new file's blob `c5752231b1e` is the blob the dev's ablation reports restoring to.
9. The store writes with the system context, so row-level security does not judge the ledger write; the two gates are the whole authority, and the engine's hooks still run (the booted pin shows the last-admin hook firing). The same shape as the flow and action stores.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/15204-s2c-catalog-activation-door.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` **minor**, `Clause-②: yes` on its own line, naming the route, body, effect, authority and refusals. Right: one additive HTTP route on the dispatcher, no existing route's contract changed. Not BREAKING.
- No other package publishes a change: `@objectstack/core` is only imported (its exports landed with stage 1); `@objectstack/client` gains no method (`server-only` row); `@objectstack/dogfood` is private; `scripts/` and the docs are repo-owned; `row-active.ts` is a comment. No further changeset is owed.
- `Clause-②: yes` matches the diff (a new write door widens the public surface's accept set) and the PR body's second line. Amendment 6101897723 asked for `yes` on 2c.
- ADR-0087 marker: none owed (no `packages/spec` disposition in the diff) and none present.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Q1 route spelling → A (6103293232).** The route as built is judged in ①.1–①.6.
2. **Q2 the stacked PR → A for #22736 (6103293232).** On this head the base is `main` and the merge round is one no-rebase merge (`638ea68d`). The PR body's first line still reads "Stacked on stage 1 … the base is `claude/issue-15204-s1-…`" and its size line names the old base: stale prose, not a published page; the follow-up push should rewrite both.
3. **`Test Core (3/6)` · `plan.boot-parity` · `sys_activity` (seat note 6104322014).** Green on this head: `Test Core (3/6)` and the `Test Core` roll-up both conclude `success` on `2c2b3f49`, after the one red on `306de5fe`. The seat note's reading (not this diff's: no object registration, boot composition or migrate code is touched, and the 14 stage-2c files are unchanged between the two heads) stands; the question of a flake in `plan.boot-parity.integration.test.ts` on a tree without this PR is `main`'s to measure, not this PR's.
4. **Docs owed this round (Landed 6104351995).** `authorization.mdx` now names the route, the body, who may call it and the 404; every sentence is true of the code. `metadata-lifecycle.mdx`: the switch sits in a sentence after the Regime C table, not in the `permission` row, and says the refusal does not name it yet. That is the dev's deviation, and it is the true shape: the table's column is "Sanctioned path the refusal names", and `PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME.permission` names only the clone (the out-of-scope finding the seat accepted in 6103293232). Answered by the seat as **C**: the `permission` regime row gets no `switchOff` (the composed refusal sentence would pass the pinned < 500-character bound of `protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts`), so the `permission` row keeps listing only what the refusal names and the switch stays in the sentence after the table, which is what this head publishes. The follow-up push on this PR adds `switchOff` to `PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME.position` only (`POST /api/v1/security/_activation/position/:name`, operator-only under a wall), with its changeset and re-pins; that delta is judged on its own head. One nit for that push: under C the word "yet" in "The refusal does not name it yet" promises a change that is not coming for `permission`. Not a FAIL reason on this head.
5. **The comment-only `row-active.ts` correction** (2a's finding, carrier 2b per 6103991518, moved to this round by 6104535364): delivered. Checked on `main`: `resolve-authz-context.ts` has no `isRowActive` reference, and each named reader has one (plugin-auth `last-admin-guard.ts`, plugin-security `explain-engine.ts` and `security-plugin.ts`, plugin-sharing `sharing-rule-service.ts`). No code or export changes; no changeset owed. The list is dated "on `main`": after 2b lands, the guard's enumeration and `readPositionActive` leave it, so the follow-up push, which merges `main` again, re-measures that list.
6. **2b × 2c pin rule (6103398921).** 2b (#22745) is ACCEPTed (6104535364) and queued, not merged at this head, so `catalog-activation-door.dogfood.test.ts` still pins stage 1's flat 403, which is true of `main` today. 2c lands second, so the follow-up push rewrites the `admin_full_access` case to the ruled pair (403 when no administrator who can sign in remains; a 200 control restored in `finally`). Landing condition: this head must not merge after #22745 does, because on that tree the booted showcase's seeded admin also owns the Default Organization and the case answers 200.
7. **Escalated: the audience anchors are switchable (①.4c).** The seat names a carrier: either the door's step 4 refuses `position/everyone` and `position/guest`, or a ruling records that the installation-wide switch covers the anchors. Non-blocking for this head.
8. **`PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME.permission` names only the clone** (dev's out-of-scope finding): accepted with no carrier in 6103293232, and under C it stays so; the `position` regime row's `switchOff` is the follow-up push's item (③.4).
9. **`check:platform-checklist`** exits 1 locally with the same ABSENT SYMBOL anchors stage 1, 2a and 2b measured identical on `main`; neither file is in this diff.
